nodes.title: Launcher: the assembled boot prompt is asserted by no cell — KS-907's fix can vanish at 18/0, and the seat sentence misled a live seat tonight
nodes.description:
**Nothing asserts what the boot prompt actually SAYS.** The launcher computes `$GIT_SYNC_STEP`, the suite reads it from a standalone marker, and the prompt the session actually receives is checked by no cell. Two consumers have now been proven wrong through that gap in one night.

## Item 1 — `$GIT_SYNC_STEP` never reaches an assertion (QA FINDING 1, MAJOR)

The `DRY_RUN` markers at `L659` print the variable **directly**. The boot prompt consumes it **separately** at `L483`. Two independent consumers of one variable; the suite reads only the first.

QA evidence — a one-line tamper (`887c3c23`) replacing `${GIT_SYNC_STEP}` at `L483` with literal text, marker untouched:

```
suite result:  18 passed, 0 FAILED   — every cell green
boot prompt:   199 lines -> 191 lines, "pull latest on the current branch" GONE
```

Proven with an instrumented pair (shipped + tampered, each printing `$INITIAL_PROMPT` under dry-run): shipped YES, tampered NO.

**Impact:** a future edit near `L483` — a 200-line block that is edited often — silently reverts KS-907 while the guard stays 18/0. KS-907 exists because a second seat's boot fast-forwarded a live branch under the first seat, before that session had read the brief telling it it was a second seat.

## Item 2 — the seat sentence reads as an assignment, and it misled a live seat tonight

Seat A was told by its boot prompt that its working copy was `worktrees/seat-b` — **this seat's worktree.** Seat A measured the pane mapping, disbelieved the launcher, and proceeded correctly as seat A; nothing was written into the wrong tree. A seat that trusted the line would have written into another live session's worktree.

Seat A's measurement, verbatim:

> pane %130 -> pane_pid 1790 -> cockpit label "Secuura/Blockchain" (no -B) = SEAT A = me
> pane %129 -> pane_pid 89454 -> cockpit label "Secuura/Blockchain-B" = SEAT B = s140e,
>             live since 22:24:23, PID 89456, working in worktrees/seat-b

**⚠️ The mechanism is NOT what it was handed to me as, and the correction changes the fix.** It was relayed as "the seat registry decides which worktree a pane is told to use, and no cell asserts the assignment is right." Measured here: **there is no assignment mechanism at all, and the registry has nothing to do with it.**

```
L344-346:  SEAT_WORKTREES="$(ls -1 "$PROJECT_DIR/worktrees" | sed 's|^|worktrees/|' ...)"
L363:      Sync YOUR OWN working copy instead${SEAT_WORKTREES:+ (this project has: ${SEAT_WORKTREES})},
```

`SEAT_WORKTREES` is a plain directory listing, **byte-identical for every pane**. `grep -c SEAT_WORKTREES` = 3, all three above. The sentence states a true fact — but its subject is *"YOUR OWN working copy"*, so a one-entry list reads as an assignment. With exactly one worktree present, that misreading is at its maximum.

The launcher says so itself at `L261`: *"The cockpit passes NOTHING that distinguishes the seats — both panes invoke a byte-identical command line."*

So this is a **wording defect plus a missing capability**, not a wrong computed value — nothing computed the wrong seat. The existing mitigation is the very next clause (*"if you have not been told which one is yours, ask before writing anywhere"*), and it worked: this seat asked, seat A measured.

**Fix shape (two options, the first is trivially safe):**

1. Reword so the list cannot read as ownership — e.g. *"this project contains the following worktrees: …; if you have not been told which is yours, ask."*
2. Actually derive the pane's seat. The cockpit label **is** reachable — it is in the parent shell's command line, which is how both seats identified themselves tonight (`ps -o command` on the launcher's own parent shows `[cockpit] Secuura/Blockchain-B exited`). That is a feature, not a guard, and it should not be attempted while two seats are live.

## Item 3 — the premise the whole registry rests on is asserted by no cell (QA NOT-TESTED 2)

The QA agent rated this **above FINDING 1**. The launcher registers `$$` and its `lstart` believing `exec` **replaces** the process, keeping pid and start time. The dry run `exit 0`s instead of exec'ing, so the entry it writes is stale the instant it is written. `exec claude … "$INITIAL_PROMPT"` (`L663`) is the only line below the dry-run exit and **is exercised by nothing** — not the suite, not the QA pass.

If that line were ever changed to anything that forks (a wrapper, `claude &`, `bash -c`), every registry entry would be invalid on arrival, the guard would silently stop working, and all 18 cells would stay green.

## Why these are one ticket

All three are the same mechanism: **a value the launcher computes correctly, consumed somewhere no cell looks.** Items 1 and 2 are literally the same variable's journey into `$INITIAL_PROMPT`; item 3 is the assumption that the prompt is ever `exec`'d at all. One fix — emit the assembled prompt behind a `DRY_RUN_INITIAL_PROMPT` marker and assert its **text** — makes all three assertable.

## Regression tests

Two cells against the assembled prompt, not the marker: empty registry -> prompt contains PULLTEXT; one live seat -> contains ROTEXT and **not** PULLTEXT. Red-proof by deleting the `L483` interpolation and requiring exactly those cells to fail. Item 2 adds a third: the prompt's named-worktree text against the pane's own cockpit label.

⚠️ **Do not fix the launcher while two seats are live.** It is live on disk under a by-hash gate; a relaunch is gated. `.pre-` restore copies exist for both files.

Sources: QA verdict `[QA -> Wednesday] Secuura SEAT B KS-911 + KS-912 (launcher, by hash)` 2026-09-06T12:18:53Z, read whole; item 2 from Wednesday's addendum quoting seat A, with the mechanism re-measured in this seat and corrected. Follows [[KS-911]] / [[KS-912]].
